overall: The AG found the Pittsfield City Council violated the Open Meeting Law by posting June 2 and June 4 notices without anticipated discussion topics in all-hours locations; a late web update did not cure it.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the City Council's June 2 and June 4 meeting notices omitted the listing of anticipated discussion topics.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law requires that a public body post notice of every meeting, and include a listing of topics that the chair reasonably anticipates will be discussed at the meeting.

allegations.summary: The notices that included the anticipated topics were posted only where the public could not see them at all hours; notices in all-hours locations lacked topics.
allegations.key_passage: The notices containing the anticipated topics were not posted in a location that was visible to the public at all hours.

allegations.summary: After the first complaint, the Council added topics to the June 4 notice on its website and bulletin board instead of cancelling and reposting it.
allegations.key_passage: amending a meeting notice within the 48 hour period to add topics that were reasonably anticipated is not sufficient to remedy the deficiencies in a meeting notice.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Council's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution the Council that similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
